race_context: The Metropolitan School District of Wayne Township serves about 15,700 students on Indianapolis' west side {chalkbeat_2026}. Shenia Suggs, previously assistant superintendent, became superintendent on Jan. 5, 2026, succeeding Jeff Butts, who led the district for 15 years {mirror_gordon}.
The board has seven members elected at large {chalkbeat_2022}. Winners take office in January and serve four-year terms ending in December 2030 {chalkbeat_2026}.

Seat count: the state list shows the at-large race as 'vote for 1', but four at-large seats are on the 2026 ballot and voters districtwide may choose candidates for all of them {chalkbeat_2026}. Only four candidates filed, so all four will be elected {chalkbeat_2026}.

All four candidates are incumbents running unopposed: board president Brandon Bowman, Raimeka Graham, Benjamin Wakefield and Mikeal Gordon {chalkbeat_2026}. Gordon was appointed in December 2025 to finish the term of longtime member Mike Nance, who died in November 2025; that term ends Dec. 31, 2026 {wayne_gordon}.

Operating referendum (Nov. 3, 2026): the district is asking voters to approve an operating levy of up to $0.70 per $100 of assessed value for up to eight years, replacing the 2019 referendum ($0.35), which expires in 2027; the district expects to certify $0.60 in the first year {wayne_referendum}. The district says the money would go to teacher recruitment and retention, safety and security, transportation, custodians, utilities and technology {wayne_referendum}.

Property-tax caps and funding (2025–2026): the district says it lost $21.3 million to the property-tax circuit breaker in 2025 and received $280 per student for operations, ranking 289th of 290 Indiana districts; it projects a $20 million shortfall for 2027–2028 if the referendum fails, which could mean closing an elementary school, larger classes and eliminating the HOSTS program {wayne_referendum}. In September 2025 the board cut planned bus purchases from 14 to 12 for 2026 after state property-tax changes reduced expected revenue growth {mirror_budget}.

Forums and differences: this guide found no candidate forum for the uncontested race. In the Chalkbeat/Mirror Indy/WFYI survey, Gordon and Wakefield said they support the referendum; Bowman and Graham did not respond {chalkbeat_2026}.
